neighbours.label: the adverb/preposition after 'go/went' in a non-directional idiom (went before, go without, going strong, goes well beyond); the + pole is directional 'go to / go off'
fire: We honour the pioneers who went before us.
It goes without saying that safety comes first.
The old band is still going strong after forty years.
Her influence goes well beyond the art world.
The case went before the Supreme Court last spring.
Many families had to go without heat that winter.
At ninety, my grandmother is still going strong.
The damage goes far deeper than the surface.
quiet: We honour the pioneers who went to the frontier.
It goes to show that safety comes first.
The old band is still going to concerts after forty years.
Her influence goes to the heart of the art world.
The case went to the lower court last spring.
Many families had to go to shelters that winter.
At ninety, my grandmother is still going to church.
The damage goes off the scale on the meter.
